text.TextBox 15: Attacks and How to Stop Them

slides.notes: Welcome everyone. In the next minutes we follow one attack from the first email to the ransom note, and show where each step can be stopped.

TextBox 13: 30% of breaches involve a third party, double the year before.
241 days on average to identify and contain a breach.
Sources: Verizon DBIR 2025; IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2025.

slides.notes: Three numbers. Ransomware is in almost half of breaches. Thirty percent involve a supplier or partner, double the year before. And it still takes about eight months to find and contain a breach.
In one year the share of breaches that involve a third party went from fifteen to thirty percent. Your security now depends on your suppliers' security too.

TextBox 11: Prepare plans, owners and offline backups before anything happens.
Every day an attacker stays inside costs more: detect and contain fast.
text.TextBox 43: Goal: contain in hours, not months

slides.notes: Incident response is a cycle of six phases: preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery and lessons learned. The fastest teams prepared before anything happened.
Detection does not need to be complex. This counts failed logins per address over five minutes and blocks anything above twenty.

text.TextBox 13: FIVE HABITS THAT STOP MOST ATTACKS
text.TextBox 28: Turn on multi-factor sign-in for email and socials
text.TextBox 30: Use a password manager, one password per site
text.TextBox 34: Install updates when your devices ask
text.TextBox 36: Report suspicious emails instead of clicking
text.TextBox 38: Zero. Every tool here has a free option.

slides.notes: Five habits. Multi-factor sign-in alone stops most stolen-password attacks. None of these cost money.
